newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish households down on national economy - poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedish households down on national economy - poll.

text.p: Swedish households were slightly more pessimistic than a year ago about the national economy but slightly more upbeat about their own, according to a new, monthly survey released by Sweden's Central Statistics Bureau (SCB) on Monday.

The number of people surveyed who thought the economic situation would worsen in the coming 12 months was about 36 percent in January compared with 39 percent in December 1996 and about 34 percent a year earlier.
SCB said about 22 percent of those questioned thought the economic situation would improve in the next 12 months.
The percentage of interviewees that thought their own households' economy would get worse in the next year was about 24 percent compared with 26 percent a month earlier and 29 percent a year earlier.
About 17 percent thought that their own households' economy would improve.
Pessimistic views on unemployment jumped from year ago levels.
Fifty percent of respondees in January thought the number of unemployed would increase over the next year. This compared with 52 percent in December and 39 percent in January 1996.
Only 12 percent thought unemployment would fall this year.

But inflation expectations continued its downward trend. The January survey found people expected prices to rise by 1.3 percent in the next 12 months compared with 1.4 percent in December and two percent a year ago.
The Consumer Confidence Indicator showed continued pessimism.
The indicator was minus nine percent in January compared to minus 10 percent in December and minus nine percent a year ago.
